essence: Six fields gave one discipline: sort every dollar by what can fail it, and decide in advance who pays when it does.
The Lab killed our own favourite fix (a 2028 hold-back, $9k of gift) and kept a cheaper one: re-measure the coupon gap in January 2031, before the range is named, for about $160.
The ladder-first structure is what every AI-assisted rival writes; Caplet's edge is the reason (her income can shrink in the same slump), where it breaks, and the two-cost range.

Jun's audit killed two of our own claims: the rising stock share is a bonds-being-spent effect, not a hook, and certainty costs nothing at the median once rivals are matched on misses; its real price is the best years.
We read how twelve real companies work (Pixar, Toyota, Amazon, Netflix and eight more) and argued for four rounds about which habits six busy Year 11s should steal.

Nine passed. The big three: whoever owns a line decides it unless it can't be undone, and then all six vote once; anyone can type "CORD:" to flag a problem at any hour, and the first reply is "thanks"; boring jobs get dealt out on Sundays instead of waiting for a volunteer.

For Caplet: our help on the IPS now gets argued and checked before it reaches you, and the research we found on how teams decide well (some of it from Wharton itself) is yours to use in the Final Report.
